idiom_name: recursive split/solve/combine on slices + a hand-pooled worker_threads / Web Worker fan-out
implementation_notes: Recursion is native - the split, base case and combine read like the textbook version - but the main thread has no CPU parallelism, so the parallel lane is hand-written: a fixed pool of worker_threads (Node) or Worker (browser) with a job queue, subranges sent by postMessage, and a join that awaits all outstanding jobs. Worker payloads are copied by structured clone unless ArrayBuffers are transferred or SharedArrayBuffer is used, so the practical structure is serialize, compute, deserialize, combine - which only pays for coarse leaves. Below the threshold, stay on the calling thread: recursion on slices is then the whole realization.
pitfalls: Messages between threads are copied, not shared: send ArrayBuffers with a transfer list or use SharedArrayBuffer, or deserialization dominates the leaf work.
Workers are expensive to start - one per subproblem is far slower than plain recursion; size a fixed pool to os.cpus().length.
SharedArrayBuffer coordination requires Atomics (Atomics.wait/notify); busy-waiting on the main thread freezes the event loop.
